title: From sample to scanned chip

blocks.what_we_do: Trace sample identity through a plate and laboratory well.
blocks.why: DNA extraction, concentration checks, amplification, fragmentation, hybridisation, staining and scanning precede the export. A plate groups laboratory wells processed together. A well can contain a technical replicate of a person. Consequently a row in a laboratory export is not always a unique person. Batch effects are systematic differences associated with processing, such as a faulty plate, rather than the phenotype of interest.
blocks.command:
```{r s1-4}
sheet <- read.csv(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "lab_export", "sample_sheet.csv"), colClasses = "character")
table(sheet$Plate)
sum(nzchar(sheet$Replicate_of))
stopifnot(nrow(sheet) == 2016L)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
Twenty-one plates, each with 96 wells, for 2,016 measurements. Sixteen wells are labelled technical replicates; 2,000 original people were simulated.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with the supplied simulated dataset.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
A plate has 96 wells and two are replicates of other wells. Must it contain 96 different people?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Wells count measurements; people count biological individuals.

</details>
